Rashi on Ketubot 26a:10:1.english: And a rumor emerged about him - A mere rumor, and not testimony.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:10:2.hebrew: ואחתיניה - מן הכהונה עד שיבדקו את הדבר, שמעלה הוא לכהונה:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:10:2.english: And we downgraded him - from the priesthood until they investigate the matter, for it is an elevated status for the priesthood.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:1:1.english: And they immersed me - Because an ordinary child plays in garbage heaps, and creeping creatures are commonly found there.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:1:2.english: In the evening - For he requires sunset.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:3:1.hebrew: והחולק בב"ד - קא ס"ד שעל פי ב"ד הקבוע בעיר היו חולקין לו תרומה בבית הגרנות, ולקמיה פריך: אי בב"ד לא הוי חזקה, היכא הויא חזקה:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:3:1.english: And one who receives a share in court - It was initially assumed that by [order of] the court established in the city they would apportion teruma to him at the threshing floors, and later [the Gemara] asks: If [receiving a share] in court does not establish a presumptive status, where is a presumptive status established?

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:5:1.hebrew: בתר דקנסינהו עזרא - ללוים דלא ליתבו להו, כדאמרי' ביבמות בפ' יש מותרות (יבמות דף פו:):
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:5:1.english: After Ezra penalized them - [He penalized] the Levites that [people] should not give [first tithe] to them, as we say in Yevamot, in the chapter [entitled] Yesh Mutarot (Yevamot 86b).

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:6:1.hebrew: לוי דלאו לוי הוא - כלומר, בלוי ליכא לספוקי, דהא אביו כהן:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:6:1.english: Levite, that he is not a Levite - That is to say, regarding [whether he is a] Levite there is no [room] to doubt, for his father is a priest.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:6:2.hebrew: למ"ד כו' - פלוגתא היא ביבמות (שם):
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:6:2.english: According to the one who says, etc. - It is a dispute in Yevamot (there).

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:7:1.english: In his father’s property, etc., [it] is not a presumptive status - To silence [the] rumor circulating against him about his mother, that she is a divorcée and he is a ḥalal.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:8:1.hebrew: פשיטא - דהא אפי' הוא חלל, יורש את אביו:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:8:1.english: [It is] obvious - For even [if] he is a chalal, he inherits his father.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:9:1.hebrew: רבן שמעון היינו רבי אליעזר - דהא ודאי במקום שיש עוררין לא אמר רבן שמעון דליהוי חד נאמן, וכי אמר מעלין במקום שאין עוררין קאמר:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:9:1.english: Rabban Shimon is [identical to] Rabbi Eliezer - For certainly, where there are challengers, Rabban Shimon did not say that one [witness] is believed; and when he said "one elevates [to the priesthood]," he said [so] where there are no challengers.

Rashi on Ketubot 26a:9:2.hebrew: דר"א סבר ערער חד - הוי ערער, ואין אחד נאמן עליו להכשירו:
Rashi on Ketubot 26a:9:2.english: That Rabbi Eliezer holds [that] a challenge [by] one [witness] - [It] constitutes a [valid] challenge, and one [witness] is not believed against it to qualify him [for the priesthood].

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:10:1.hebrew: ואתא עד אחד ואמר ידענא ביה דכהן הוא - לא בעי למימר דפליגי אי מעלין ע"פ עד אחד כשהקול פוסל, דפשיטא ליה להש"ס דלא פסיל קול לכ"ע כיון דאיכא עד וחזקה; ועוד, דקול לא הוי קרי עוררין:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:10:1.english: And one witness came and said: "I know that he is a priest" - [The Gemara] did not want to say that they disagree [over] whether we elevate [him to the priesthood] on the basis of one witness when a rumor disqualifies [him], because it is obvious to the Gemara that a rumor does not disqualify [him] according to everyone, since there is [both] a witness and a presumptive status [of priesthood]; and furthermore, [the Mishnah] would not call a rumor "challengers."

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:1:1.hebrew: במסיח לפי תומו - וא"ת: ומנ"ל דהכי הוא? דלמא ר' חייא העלה בן על פי אביו במסיח לפי תומו, ורבי העלה אח ע"פ אחיו אפי' בלא מסיח! ואר"י: דמסתמא דבמאי דקתני בברייתא מילתא דרבי, עשה רבי מעשה. ועוד: דאי אפשר דרבי העלה אח ע"פ אחיו ללויה אפילו בלא מסיח, דהתם אין שייך לומר שבידו להאכילו מעשר, למ"ד מעשר ראשון מותר לזרים:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:1:1.english: When he speaks offhandedly - And if you ask: From where do we know that this is so? Perhaps Rabbi Ḥiyya elevated a son based on his father's [testimony only] when speaking offhandedly, whereas Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] elevated a brother based on his brother's [testimony] even without speaking offhandedly! And R"Y answers: Presumably, in that which the baraita teaches as the statement of Rabbi, Rabbi [himself] acted [in accordance with it]. And furthermore, it is impossible that Rabbi elevated a brother based on his brother's [testimony] to Levitehood even without speaking offhandedly, because there it is not applicable to say that it is in his power to feed him tithe, according to the one who says that first tithe is permitted to non-Levites [zarim].

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:1:2.hebrew: מבית הספר - נקט שלא לומר שהוא עבד, כדאמר בסוף פירקין (לקמן כתובות דף כח.):
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:1:2.english: From school - [He] mentioned [this] so that one would not say that he was a slave, as it states at the end of our chapter (below, Ketubot 28a).

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:5:1.hebrew: אין בתר דקנסינהו עזרא - ולר"ע, דקודם קנסא הוי דוקא ללוי — בתר קנסא אף לכהנים; אבל לר"א בן עזריה, דמקמי קנסא הוי אף לכהן — בתר קנסא הוי לכהן דוקא. והא דמעשר ראשון חזקה לכהונה, אתיא כר' אלעזר בן עזריה ולא כר"ע. ויש שמוחקין "אין", ומפרשים דהא דקאמר "בתר דקנסינהו עזרא" הוי אפי' לר"ע, דבתר קנסא הוי לכ"ע לכהן דוקא, והוי כמו "אלא". ושיבוש הוא בידם! דהא בכמה מקומות מוכיח דמעשר ראשון ללוי אף בתר קנסא, כדתנן בפ' כל הגט (גיטין דף ל.): "המלוה מעות את הכהן ואת הלוי להיות מפריש עליהן כו'"; וכן התם בגמרא: "ישראל שאמר לבן לוי כור מעשר לאביך בידי"; ובפ' הזרוע (חולין קלא: ושם) פריך: "מעשר ראשון דלוי הוא"; וכן בכמה מקומות — והיינו כר"ע. ועוד, דלמ"ד קנסא לעניים, היכי הוי חזקה לכהונה? דאליבא דר"ע פליגי בס"פ יש מותרות (יבמות פו: ושם), דאיכא למ"ד קנסא לכהנים ואיכא למ"ד לעניים. דלר' אלעזר בן עזריה הוי דוקא לכהן ואפי' לעשירים, כמו קודם קנסא, דלא קנסם עזרא שהרי עלו. ולמ"ד קנסא לעניים, משמע התם דוקא לעניים ולא לכהנים עשירים, אפי' בימי טומאה, דלית ליה דבימי טומאה עניים הוו. ועניים דהתם אין לפרש עניי לויים דוקא ולא עניי ישראל וכהנים, דא"כ נשתכרו עניי לויים במה שלא עלו! ועוד, דמשמע התם: אילו הוו כהנים בימי טומאתם עניים, לכ"ע הוו שקלי, אע"ג דלענין חלוקת מעשר הוו כישראל, דללוי ולא לכהן קאמר — אלא לעניים, בין עניי כהנים בין עניי לויים. ולמ"ד מעשר ראשון מותר לזרים, שקלי אפילו עניי ישראל; אבל למ"ד אסור לזרים, אין נראה שינתן לעניי ישראל כדי למוכרו, דמילתא דאתי לידי תקלה לא אתקינו רבנן, דאיכא למיחש דלמא אתי למיכליה [כדאמר בסמוך: לא מיבעיא לר"מ דאמר אסור לזרים כו']. ולר"ע לא הפקיע עזרא את הלויים מכל וכל להשוותן לישראל וכהנים, שלא יטלו עשירים לויים אלא עניי לויים בתורת עניות; אלא ללויים, בין עניים בין עשירים, היו חולקים לעולם, כדמוכח בכל הנהו שהבאתי, שהיו נוטלין בתורת לויות. ועוד, דר"ג בספינה, שנתן מעשר ראשון לר' יהושע בן חנניא (מעשר שני פ"ה מ"ט) — אי בתורת עניות יהיב ליה, אמאי לא יהב ליה נמי מעשר עני? שהרי מעשר עני נתן לר"ע! ומיהו יש לדחות דלעולם בתורת עניות נתן לו, ומה שלא נתן לו מעשר עני — לפי שהיו לו מאתים זוז, דאינו נוטל במעשר עני כדתנן במסכת פאה (פ"ח מ"ח); אבל מעשר ראשון יטול אפי' יש לו מאתים זוז, דהא איכא למ"ד דאפי' כהנים עשירים בימי טומאה עניים נינהו. ועוד, דלא רצה ליתן כל מתנותיו לעני אחד:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:5:1.english: Yes, after Ezra penalized them - According to R. Akiva, [who holds] that before the penalty it was exclusively for a Levite, after the penalty [it was given] to priests as well. But according to R. Elazar ben Azaryah, [who holds] that prior to the penalty it was also for a priest, after the penalty it is exclusively for a priest. And this [statement of our Gemara] that first tithe is a presumption of priesthood follows R. Elazar ben Azaryah and not R. Akiva. There are some who erase [the word] "Yes," and explain that what [the Gemara] says, "after Ezra penalized them," applies even according to R. Akiva — that after the penalty, according to everyone, it is exclusively for a priest — and it is like [saying] "rather." And this is a mistaken reading in their hands, for in several places it is proven that first tithe [still goes] to a Levite even after the penalty, as we learned in the Mishnah in Chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 30a): "One who lends money to a priest or to a Levite to set aside [terumah or tithes] on their behalf, etc."; and likewise there in the Gemara: "An Israelite who said to a Levite, 'I have a kor of tithe belonging to your father in my possession'"; and in Chapter HaZeroa (Chullin 131b, and there [in the parallel]) [the Gemara] objects: "First tithe belongs to the Levite!" And so in several places — and this is in accordance with R. Akiva. Furthermore, according to the one who says the penalty [gave first tithe] to the poor, how could it be a presumption of priesthood? For according to R. Akiva they disagree at the end of Chapter Yesh Mutarot (Yevamot 86b, and there [in the parallel]), where there is one who says the penalty [gave it] to priests and there is one who says [it gave it] to the poor. For according to R. Elazar ben Azaryah it is exclusively for a priest, and even for wealthy ones, just as before the penalty — for Ezra did not penalize them, since they went up [to the Land of Israel]. And according to the one who says the penalty [gave it] to the poor, it is implied there [that it is] exclusively for the poor and not for wealthy priests, even during their days of ritual impurity, for he does not hold that during their days of impurity they are considered poor. And "the poor" mentioned there cannot be explained as referring exclusively to poor Levites and not poor Israelites and priests, for if so, poor Levites would have profited from the fact that they did not go up! Moreover, it is implied there that if priests during their days of impurity were [considered] poor, according to everyone they would take [first tithe], even though with respect to the distribution of tithe they are like Israelites, since [Scripture] says "to the Levite" and not "to the priest" — rather, [it was given] to the poor, whether poor priests or poor Levites. And according to the one who says first tithe is permitted to non-priests, even poor Israelites take it. But according to the one who says it is forbidden to non-priests, it does not seem [right] that it would be given to poor Israelites in order to sell it, because the Rabbis did not institute something that could lead to a stumbling block, as there is room for concern that perhaps they might come to eat it [as [the Gemara] says shortly below: "Needless to say according to R. Meir, who says it is forbidden to non-priests, etc."]. And according to R. Akiva, Ezra did not expropriate [first tithe from] the Levites completely to make them equal to Israelites and priests — such that wealthy Levites would not take it, only poor Levites by way of charity — rather, to the Levites, both poor and wealthy, they would always distribute it, as is proven from all those [sources] that I cited, that they would take it by virtue of their Levite status. Furthermore, [consider the incident of] Rabban Gamliel on the ship, who gave first tithe to R. Yehoshua ben Chananya (Ma'aser Sheni 5:9): if he gave it to him by way of charity, why did he not also give him the poor man's tithe, since he gave the poor man's tithe to R. Akiva? However, one can reject [this proof, and say] that indeed he gave it to him by way of charity, and the reason he did not give him the poor man's tithe is because [R. Yehoshua] had two hundred zuz, so he may not take from the poor man's tithe, as we learned in Tractate Pe'ah (8:8); whereas first tithe he may take even if he has two hundred zuz, for there is an opinion that even wealthy priests during their days of impurity are considered poor. And furthermore, [it may be] that he did not want to give all his gifts to a single poor person.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:5:2.hebrew: בתר דקנסינהו עזרא - לא אשכחן בהדיא בקרא דקנסינהו, רק מצינו בעזרא (נחמיה י): "והיה הכהן בן אהרן עם הלוים בעשר הלוים", ואיכא למימר דה"ק: כשיבאו הלוים לחלוק בבית הגרנות, יבאו הכהנים עמהם. ומיהו לר"א בן עזריה, דבתר קנסא דוקא לכהן, לא משמע מהאי קרא; דליכא למימר "עם הלוים" דקאמר קרא היינו לקבל מהם מעשר ראשון משלהם, דהא משלהם לא קנסם עזרא, כדמוכח בפרק הזרוע (חולין קלא:). וי"ל דלר"א בן עזריה לא נמנעו הלוים מכל וכל מלילך לבית הגרנות לחלוק במעשר, כדאמר בסמוך: "דלמא איקרי ויהיב ליה", כל שכן בימי עזרא שעדיין לא פשט הקנס שהיו הולכים בבית הגרנות, ולכך נאמר שילכו הכהנים עם הלוים. ולמ"ד קנסא לעניים, הא דכתיב "והיה הכהן" היינו בכהן עני; ומשום דכהנים עניים שכיחי טפי, לפי שאין כל כך עסוקים במלאכה אלא בעבודת בית המקדש וגם אין להם קרקעות, נקט כהן, וה"ה עניי ישראל למ"ד מעשר ראשון מותר לזרים. וה"ר יוסף פירש מדכתיב (במלאכי ג): "הביאו את כל המעשר אל בית האוצר" — דבית האוצר היה לשכה שתיקן עזרא לתת שם תרומת הכהנים, כדכתיב בעזרא (נחמיה י); וכיון שאומר להביא שם המעשר, א"כ של כהנים הוא, וקיימא לן (מגילה דף טו.) דמלאכי זה עזרא. ולמ"ד לעניים, נקט "אל בית האוצר" משום דכהנים עניים שכיחי טפי כדפרישית; אי נמי, "אל בית האוצר" — לא ליתן לכהנים, אלא לחלק לעניים. וה"ר אלחנן הקשה: דבסוף עזרא משמע שהמעשר היה ללוים, דכתיב: "ואדע כי מניות הלוים לא נתנה (להם) ויברחו איש לשדהו הלוים והמשוררים כו'", משמע שהלוים והמשוררים היו חולקים. וצריך לומר דזה היה מקמי דקנסינהו עזרא, אך קראי לא מוכחי הכי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:5:2.english: After Ezra penalized them - We do not find explicitly in Scripture that he penalized them; we only find in Ezra (Nehemiah 10[:39]): "And the priest, the son of Aaron, shall be with the Levites when the Levites take tithes," and one can say that this is what it means: when the Levites come to receive their share at the threshing floor, the priests shall come with them. However, according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah, [who holds] that after the penalty [first tithe is given] specifically to a priest, this is not implied by this verse; for one cannot say that "with the Levites" that the verse states means to receive first tithe from their own [produce], since Ezra did not penalize them regarding their own [produce], as is proven in the chapter [entitled] HaZero'a (Chullin 131b). And one can answer that according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah, the Levites did not refrain altogether from going to the threshing floor to receive a share of the tithe, as [the Gemara] says immediately below: "Perhaps by happenstance one gave him [first tithe]"; all the more so in the days of Ezra, when the penalty had not yet spread, they would go to the threshing floor, and therefore it was stated that the priests should go with the Levites. And according to the one who says [that] the penalty was [to give first tithe] to the poor, that which is written, "And the priest... shall be," refers to a poor priest; and because poor priests are more common — since they are not as engaged in [ordinary] labor, but rather in the Temple service, and also they have no land — it specifically mentions a priest, and the same law applies to poor Israelites according to the one who says first tithe is permitted to non-priests. And Rabbi Yosef explained [that it is derived] from what is written (in Malachi 3[:10]): "Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse" — for the storehouse was a chamber that Ezra established to place there the terumah of the priests, as is written in Ezra (Nehemiah 10[:39]); and since it says to bring the tithe there, it follows that it belongs to the priests, and we hold (Megillah 15a) that Malachi is Ezra. And according to the one who says [that it is given] to the poor, it mentions "into the storehouse" because poor priests are more common, as I have explained; alternatively, "into the storehouse" [was] not to give [it] to the priests, but rather to distribute [it] to the poor. And Rabbi Elchanan raised a difficulty: for at the end of Ezra [Nehemiah 13:10] it is implied that the tithe belonged to the Levites, as it is written: "And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given (to them); so that the Levites and the singers... were fled every one to his field, etc.," which implies that the Levites and the singers used to receive [their] shares. And one must say that this was before Ezra penalized them, though the verses do not prove this.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:9:1.hebrew: והאמר רבי יוחנן דברי הכל אין ערער כו' - נראה לר"י דר' יוחנן עיקר דבריו על משנתנו, ולהכי לא קא משני הכא: "ה"מ היכא דאיכא חזקה דכשרות כו'", כדמשני בפרק עשרה יוחסין (קדושין דף עג:). ואם תאמר: והואיל ואמתני' קאי, היכי פריך מיניה התם ובפרק קמא דגיטין (דף ט.) גבי גט — דלמא הא דקאמר ר' יוחנן דלא מהני ערער דחד, היינו היכא דאיכא עד אחד דמכשר, דקתני "מעלין לכהונה על פי עד אחד"? ויש לומר: דהש"ס ידע דר' יוחנן אמסקנא דיבר, דבתחלה היה קול, ואח"כ בא עד אחד להכשירו ולהסיר הקול, ואתו בי תרי ואמרי דבן גרושה ובן חלוצה הוא — דבכי האי גוונא א"ר יוחנן דבעינן שנים, אע"ג דהעד שהכשיר והקול כמאן דליתנהו דמי, שהרי העד גרוע מן הקול, אי לאו משום חזקה דמסייע ליה לבטל הקול, שהרי הקול פוסל והעד אינו פוסל לרבי יוחנן:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:9:1.english: And didn't Rabbi Yoḥanan say: Everyone agrees there is no challenge [with fewer than two] etc. - It appears to the Ri that the primary context of Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement is our Mishnah, and therefore [the Gemara] here does not answer, "This applies where there is a presumption of fitness etc.," as it answers in the chapter [entitled] Asarah Yuchasin (Kiddushin 73b). And if you will say: Since [Rabbi Yoḥanan's statement] refers to our Mishnah, how does [the Gemara] raise an objection from it there [in Kiddushin] and in the first chapter of Gittin (9a) regarding a bill of divorce — perhaps that which Rabbi Yoḥanan said, that a challenge of one [witness] is not effective, applies [only] where there is one witness who declares him fit, as [the Mishnah] teaches, "One elevates [a man] to the priesthood on the basis of one witness"? And one can answer: The Talmud knew that Rabbi Yoḥanan spoke with reference to the conclusion [of our Mishnah's case], where initially there was a rumor [against his lineage], and afterward one witness came to declare him fit and to remove the rumor, and then two [other] people come and say that he is the son of a divorced woman or the son of a chalutzah — for in such a case Rabbi Yoḥanan said that we require two [witnesses], even though the witness who declared him fit and the rumor are considered as if they do not exist, since the [single] witness is weaker than the rumor, were it not for the presumption [of fitness] that assists him to nullify the rumor, since a rumor disqualifies whereas a [single] witness does not disqualify according to Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:9:2.hebrew: אין ערער פחות משנים - לאפוקי חד דלא הוי ערער, אבל קול נמי פוסל בתחלה בתרומה קודם שבא העד המכשיר:
Tosafot on Ketubot 26a:9:2.english: There is no challenge [with] fewer than two [witnesses] - [This comes] to exclude one [witness], as [one] does not constitute a challenge; however, a rumor also disqualifies [him] initially from [eating] terumah before the validating witness comes.
